title: Kepler watch — sprint quicklog and temporary runbook
content:
PURPOSE
A compact, sprint-focused on-call quicklog for Kepler region (short-term). This is intentionally lightweight — the idea is to capture transient mitigations, recent patterns, and a minimal checklist for the person taking the next watch. Keep it short, add links, escalate if unsure.

SUMMARY (toplines)
- Major risk vectors this sprint: bursty traffic from model-eval jobs, ephemeral pod OOMs on quantized variants, cache thrash on long-tail prefixes.
- Known degraded paths: small percentage (~0.8%) of gptq-5b-qa requests hit an older kernel causing latency jumps; fallback route enabled for 02:00–06:00 PST.
- Current capacity headroom: dedicated pool Kepler-GPU-1 at ~72% util; can burst to spare nodes but cold-start penalty ~350ms for first requests.

WHAT I DID BEFORE HANDOFF (quick chronicle)
- 2026-02-19 21:10 PST: Saw latency spike on /v1/generate; traced to model selector returning quantized-gptq-5b-old (kernel mismatch). Created INC-3421, applied temporary routing rule to route queries > 512 tokens to gptq-5b-stable.
- 2026-02-20 03:05 PST: Redis KV cache eviction rate spiked after a workload with long shared prefixes. Increased cache retention for Kepler namespace (temp) and filed GH PR-879 to adjust cache heuristics.
- Ran smoke test of failover path (region fallback to ashby) — 7/8 checks passed (one mismatch in tokenization test).

QUICK HITS (what to watch in the first 30m)
- Grafana dashboards: kepler/latency/p50,p95; kepler/errors/5xx; kepler/cache/eviction-rate.
- Pager rules: page on sustained p95 > 600ms for 2m OR 5xx rate > 1% for 1m.
- Slack channels: #kepler-watch (primary). If paging, escalate to @sre-lead.
- Synthetics: run synth full-sweep if p95 > 400ms. Command: curl -sS https://synth-runner.internal/run?profile=kepler-full

TEMP MITIGATIONS (short-term playbook fragments)
- If kernel mismatch appears (symptom: latency spike + kernel mismatch logs in /var/log/inference/runtime):
  1) Enable fallback route: api call to routing service -> PUT /routes/kepler/fallback {"from":"gptq-5b-old","to":"gptq-5b-stable"}
  2) Restart warmers for affected pool: kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/warmer-kepler-gpu-1
  3) Open INC and tag with "kepler-kernel-mismatch".
- If cache eviction rate > 200 req/s sustained:
  1) Increase retention: redis-cli -h cache-kepler acl setuser kepler-temp-policy "on" (infra will revert after 12h)
  2) Throttle evaluation jobs: patch evaluation job replicas to 0.2 (linear backoff) — see GH PR-879.
- If 5xx > 1%: enable canary fallback to ashby region: Send request to ops-api /v1/route/fallback?region=ashby&window=30m

SHORT COMMANDS (copypasta)
- Check p95: curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=kepler.latency.p95 | jq .value
- Re-route rule (example): http POST https://routing.internal/api/routes Authorization:"Bearer $TOKEN" name="kepler-temp" target:=\'{"from":"gptq-5b-old","to":"gptq-5b-stable"}\'
- Restart warmer: kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/warmer-kepler-gpu-1

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (for follow-up)
- How much did the cache tweaks actually reduce end-to-end latency? Need a postmortem metric patch (compare 2026-02-19 20:00–23:00 window). Assigned: @Marta.
- Longer-term: schedule a kernel upgrade for gptq-5b-old nodes AND a canary for tokenization tests to avoid mismatch. Ticket: RFC-KERNEL-KEPLER.
- Evaluate whether synthetic load tests should run staggered to avoid simultaneous cache churn.

POST-SHIFT HANDOVER (what to leave for next shift)
- Leave synth job running for 1h after leaving if p95 between 300–500ms. Note results in thread and tag "kepler-watch:handoff-result".
- If you made any routing changes, add a short note in Slack and tag @oncall-rotations so infra knows to rollback or formalize.

NOTES TO SELF (rough)
- The temporary retention change is noisy in metrics — watch prometheus for increased memory usage, may need to revert earlier.
- When opening an INC, include the failure curl (with obfuscated tokens) and the warmers' pod names. Saves time.

QUICK LOG (timestamped entries to add during shift)
- 2026-02-20 04:12 PST: synth returned 502 for model gptq-5b-stable on one node -> restarted warmers (ok).
- 2026-02-20 05:01 PST: eviction rate down 45% after retention bump.
- [space for you to add your own bullets]

ESCALATION MATRIX (abridged)
- Oncall -> if unable to remediate in 20m or cross-team required, escalate to SRE lead (Slack + call).
- If customer-impacting (>=1 active user-visible outage), page product incident manager and start conference bridge.

FINAL THOUGHTS
This is intentionally condensed — use it as a living scratchpad and delete outdated short-term fixes. If you formalize a mitigation, move it into ops runbooks and update Confluence link above.

-- Priya
